title: HadesMiMC Full-Data Gröbner-Basis Security Conjecture
summary: The source conjectures a sufficient full-round security bound, motivated by tests in which attack complexity was lowest with one plaintext–ciphertext pair when alpha equaled three; prove or refute it.

formal_statement.body:
For a HadesMiMC parameter set $(N,\alpha,t,R_P,R_F)$, with $R_F$ denoting the number of full rounds, prove or refute the conjecture that HadesMiMC is secure against the full-data variant of the Gröbner-basis attack whenever

$$R_F \ge 2+\log_{\alpha}(2)\cdot\left\lceil\frac{N+2\log_2(t+R_P)-2\log_2(t)}{2t+R_P}\right\rceil.$$

The motivating observation is that, in all practically tested instances with $\alpha=3$, the attack's computational complexity was minimized by using a single plaintext–ciphertext pair.

scope.domain: This concerns algebraic cryptanalysis of HadesMiMC against full-data Gröbner-basis attacks.
parameters: N, alpha, t, and R_P: HadesMiMC parameters appearing in the conjectured bound
alpha equal to three: tested value in the motivating observation
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or refute that HadesMiMC is secure against the full-data variant of the Gröbner-basis attack whenever the stated lower bound on R_F holds.

citations.label: On a Generalization of Substitution-Permutation Networks: The HADES Design Strategy

progress.summary: The source presents the claim explicitly as a conjecture, after reporting that all practically tested instances with alpha equal to three had minimum attack complexity with a single plaintext–ciphertext pair. It leaves security under the stated full-round condition to proof or refutation.
